drivingQuestion: How would the first tanna answer Rabbi Meir's claim that the husband does not want a shaven wife?
outcomeNote: explains both sides of the mishna's dispute without deciding

segments.he: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא אָמַר לָךְ: אֶפְשָׁר בְּפֵאָה נׇכְרִית. וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר: בְּפֵאָה נׇכְרִית, אַיְּידֵי דְּזוּהֲמָא — לָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara analyzes these opinions: «And the first tanna» could have «said to you» in response to Rabbi Meir’s argument: It is «possible» for her to compensate «by» wearing «a wig,» and therefore she would not appear shaven, and her husband would have no cause for complaint. «And Rabbi Meir holds:» As for compensating «by» wearing «a wig, since» it is «dirty he is not amenable» to this solution, and he may therefore nullify her vow.
